title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Fuse the inverse RoPE into the sparse decode reduce
body_opening:
## Purpose

The ROCm sparse decode writes the attention output twice. The reduce kernel
combines the split-K partials and stores `[T, H, 512]`, and then
`_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` reads that whole tensor back, rotates the trailing
64 rope lanes and writes it out again — a full round trip per layer, for an
epilogue on data the reduce already held in registers.

From a 10-step decode trace on MI355X (TP4, rank 0):

| kernel | total | calls | share of kernel time |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_sparse_attn_decode_gfx950_partial_kernel` | 4707.3 us | 430 | 3.24% |
| `_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel` | 2214.2 us | 430 | 1.52% |
| `_inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` | 1965.5 us | 430 | 1.35% |

body_opening:
## Purpose

`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla` cannot be selected on ROCm at all today. The pack in `_fp32x2_to_fp4x2` is PTX, `f` is not an AMDGPU asm constraint, and every worker aborts during startup with `unknown asm constraint 'f'`. title: Add separate post-thinking sampling parameters
body_opening:
## Summary

This PR adds support for using a separate set of sampling parameters after a model finishes its `<think>...</think>` reasoning block.

The primary motivation is models such as **Qwen 3.8 27B**, where the optimal sampling parameters for reasoning differ substantially from the optimal parameters for the final answer.

In testing, Qwen 3.8 27B benefits from a relatively high temperature (`~0.9–1.0`) during reasoning. Lower temperatures can cause the reasoning process to become repetitive or enter loops. However, keeping that same temperature after `</think>` noticeably reduces the reliability and precision of the final response, including normal chat output and tool calls.

title: [AMD] Deepen the top-k v2 streaming load pipeline on ROCm
body_opening:
## Motivation

On ROCm, the top-k v2 streaming kernel reads the input one 16B vector at a time. Each
iteration is load -> classify -> LDS atomic, so the next load cannot start until the
previous one lands. The grid is one block per row, so at decode batch sizes most CUs sit
idle and there is no other work to hide that load latency behind.

Keeping a second vector in flight fills the gap. This is the same change that helped the
legacy AOT top-k kernel (`elementwise/topk.cu`) on gfx950.
